    # ending with j open brackets

    # Prefix sum array to quickly calculate the number of valid sequences
    prefix_sum = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(2 * n + 1)]
    for i in range(2 * n + 1):
        for j in range(n + 1):
            prefix_sum[i][j] = (prefix_sum[i - 1][j] + prefix_sum[i][j - 1]) % MOD
    
    # Count the number of valid sequences of length 2n
    total_sequences = prefix_sum[2 * n][n]
    
    # Now, we need to subtract the number of valid sequences that do not contain s
    # We will use a similar DP approach but this time we will keep track of the position
    # in the substring s that we have matched so far
    
    # dp2[i][j][k] will store the number of ways to form a valid sequence of length i
    # ending with j open brackets and having matched k characters of s
    dp2 = [[[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)] for _ in range(2 * n + 1)]
    dp2[0][0][0] = 1
    
    for i in range(2 * n + 1):
        for j in range(n + 1):
            for k in range(m + 1):
                if i > 0 and j > 0:
                    dp2[i][j][k] = (dp2[i][j][k] + dp2[i - 1][j - 1][k]) % MOD
                if i > 0 and j < n:
                    dp2[i][j][k] = (dp2[i][j][k] + dp2[i - 1][j + 1][k]) % MOD
                if i > 0 and k < m and (s[k] == '(' and j > 0 or s[k] == ')' and j < n):
                    dp2[i][j][k + 1] = (dp2[i][j][k + 1] + dp2[i - 1][j][k]) % MOD
    
    # The number of valid sequences of length 2n that contain s
    sequences_with_s = dp2[2 * n][n][m]
    
    # The result is the total number of valid sequences minus those that do not contain s
    result = (total_sequences - sequences_with_s + MOD) % MOD
    
    return result
